answer: Sequential verifiable delay functions resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to compute an unparallelizable chain of modular squarings bound to its key and the epoch's randomness beacon. Every fake identity requires a dedicated execution lane, consuming single-thread silicon, copper cooling overhead, and continuous power while unverified keys sit as inert as onyx. However, adversaries with custom squaring ASICs can still run large fleets cheaply when energy prices hit their nadir.
